chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A slave who is freed on the Day of 'Arafah.' He said: 'If one attains one of the two stations, then he has attained the Hajj.'

key_terms.المَوقِفَيْنِ: The two stations (referring to the two essential components or times of Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: Day of 'Arafah, the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a slave on the Day of 'Arafah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a slave manumitted on the Day of 'Arafah is considered to have completed their Hajj obligation, highlighting the immense spiritual weight of emancipation in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the concept that specific acts of worship can substitute for or fulfill the core requirements of Hajj, reflecting the flexibility within the Shia legal tradition regarding the conditions of Hajj validity.
